Data quality / Trust and coverage

Data freshness within SLA

A configured reliability measure of expected dataset checks that satisfy their maximum permitted data age. For example, a sales dashboard may require source event watermarks less than two hours old during operating hours.

How we use it

We expose the last source watermark, last successful sync, and freshness alert so decision makers can see whether a dashboard reflects current activity.

Transparent calculationScheduled expected checks meeting their dataset freshness threshold ÷ all scheduled expected checks due in the period × 100

46 ÷ 48 × 100 = approximately 95.83% freshness-SLA compliance.

Break the result down

  • Dataset and freshness SLA
  • Source and ingestion schedule
  • Check period and failure reason

Questions we investigate

  • Which datasets exceed their agreed freshness threshold?
  • Are missing checks counted as expected failures?
  • Is delay caused by source updates or ingestion?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Inspect upstream and ingestion timestamps.
  • Set dataset-specific thresholds and alert owners.
  • Review missed checks and recover delayed loads.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Data platform operations lead
At scheduled checks with daily exception review.

Required data

  • All scheduled expected check records
  • Dataset update timestamps and freshness thresholds
  • Check clock, schedule, and missing-check policy

Read the measure with context

Zero expected checks makes the rate undefined. Missing checks must not count as passes. A recent refresh timestamp can still load stale source data. Thresholds depend on source cadence and time zone; an intentionally quiet source needs a defined heartbeat or freshness policy.
